   - Guidance/modeling and boundaries (authoritative parenting) versus coercion and punishment (authoritarian parenting) are different processes with different outcomes.
   - Forcing can be behavioral compliance without internal acceptance; encouragement and reasoning can produce internalized values.

   - Research on parenting styles (e.g., authoritative vs authoritarian) suggests high warmth + appropriate structure (authoritative) tends to predict better long-term outcomes (academic success, social competence, mental health).

- Parenting style research (e.g., distinctions among authoritarian, authoritative, permissive) generally finds that authoritative parenting — high warmth combined with reasonable structure and autonomy support — produces the best broad outcomes (academic, social, wellbeing) in many contexts. - Cross-cultural research shows variation: in some collectivist cultures, stronger parental control does not always predict poor outcomes, possibly because control is embedded within a framework of parental warmth and shared values.
